subject: general
question:
Which of the following is the correct balanced equation for the given chemical reaction?

Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂
solution:
The correct answer is __**3Fe(s) + 4H2O(g) → Fe3O4(s) + 4H2(g)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• To balance the given chemical reaction, the number of atoms of each element on the reactant side must equal the number of atoms of each element on the product side.
 
• For the correct balanced equation: 3 moles of iron (Fe) react with 4 moles of water (H2O) to produce 1 mole of iron(II,III) oxide (Fe3O4) and 4 moles of hydrogen gas (H2).
 
• In the equation, the iron atoms are balanced: 3 Fe atoms on the reactant side and 3 Fe atoms in Fe3O4 on the product side.
 
• The hydrogen atoms are balanced: 8 H atoms on the reactant side (from 4 H2O) and 8 H atoms on the product side (from 4 H2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balancing Chemical Equations:**

 
 
• Chemical equations must be balanced to obey the Law of Conservation of Mass, which states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• To balance a chemical equation, adjust the coefficients (the numbers in front of the chemical formulas) to ensure the same number of each type of atom on both sides of the equation.
 
• Start by balancing the atoms of elements that appear in only one reactant and one product.
 
• Balance the atoms of elements that appear in multiple reactants or products last.
 
 
 
• **Iron(II,III) Oxide (Fe3O4):**
 
 
• Iron(II,III) oxide, also known as magnetite, is a mixed oxide of iron where iron exists in both +2 and +3 oxidation states.
 
• It is a black, magnetic mineral that is a common iron ore used in the production of iron and steel.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas (H2):**
 
 
• Hydrogen gas is a colorless, odorless, highly flammable diatomic gas.
 
• It is the lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe, primarily found in stars and gas giant planets.
 
• Hydrogen gas is used in various industrial processes, including the production of ammonia for fertilizers and the hydrogenation of fats and oils.
